title: HCLTech Signs Anthropic Pact, Will Build Dedicated Agentic AI Business Unit
excerpt: India's third-largest IT services firm will set up a centre of excellence to build enterprise AI-agent solutions around Claude, Cowork and Claude Code, with safety and governance as stated priorities.
body:
• HCLTech signed a partnership with Anthropic on October 12 to accelerate enterprise adoption of agentic AI.
  • The company will create a dedicated business unit with a centre of excellence to build agentic AI solutions.
  • Its teams will embed Anthropic products — Claude, Cowork and Claude Code — into industry-specific solutions, with a focus on safety, cybersecurity and governance.
  • The announcement lands the same day HCLTech reports its second-quarter results.

A business unit, not just a reseller deal

HCLTech, India's third-largest IT services company, signed a partnership with Anthropic on Monday to accelerate enterprise adoption of agentic AI, Reuters reported from Bengaluru. Rather than simply reselling the US lab's models, HCLTech will establish a dedicated business unit with a centre of excellence tasked with building agentic AI solutions for enterprise clients.

https://x.com/tylerx_durden/status/2109653589626962108

Under the arrangement, HCLTech teams will build industry solutions and embed Anthropic's products — the Claude models, Cowork and Claude Code — into client workflows. Reporting on the pact also notes Claude models being integrated into HCLTech's own Agent Studio and AI Force platforms, which coordinate enterprise workflows run by AI agents.

Why safety and governance lead the pitch

The partnership is explicitly framed around safety, cybersecurity and governance — the three objections that most often stall AI-agent deployments inside banks, insurers, hospitals and manufacturers. That positioning fits Anthropic's brand as the safety-focused frontier lab, and it fits HCLTech's client base of heavily regulated enterprises that need audit trails and controls before they let agents touch production systems.

For India's IT majors, pacts like this are the industry's answer to a hard question: if AI agents write code and run workflows, what happens to the outsourcing model built on headcount? The emerging answer is to sell the agents, the integration and the governance layer — higher-value work, but work that rewards engineers who can design and supervise AI systems rather than only execute tasks.

What to watch

HCLTech announces its second-quarter results later on Monday, when investors will press management on how quickly the Anthropic unit can convert into revenue and how it sits alongside the firm's other AI partnerships. Rivals TCS, Infosys and Wipro have struck similar alliances with US AI labs; the differentiator will be which firm turns pilots into production deployments first. Details of the partnership are in the Reuters report.

How the unit is likely to work

A centre of excellence, in IT-services practice, is the team that sets the templates everyone else reuses: reference architectures for agents, evaluation and safety checklists, and the governance paperwork a regulated client needs before sign-off. Building that layer once, around a single model family, is cheaper than improvising it project by project — and it is the part of the stack a client cannot easily swap out, which is precisely why services firms compete to own it. Embedding Claude Code into delivery teams also changes the economics of the work itself: if an AI assistant drafts and tests code under an engineer's supervision, the firm sells outcomes and oversight rather than hours. HCLTech's framing of the unit around agentic AI — systems that plan and execute multi-step tasks, not just answer questions — puts it on the side of that shift where the budgets are growing fastest.

The announcement's timing is also deliberate. Landing the pact on results day gives management a forward story to set against the quarter's numbers, and gives investors a concrete marker — a named unit, a named partner, named products — against which to measure the company's AI claims in coming quarters.
